title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Regulations on the Work of Special Supervisors of the Supreme People's Court (Trial)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Working Regulations of the Supreme People's Court on Special Supervisors (Trial)

Fa Fa [2009] No. 51

To: All High People's Courts of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Working Regulations of the Supreme People's Court on Special Supervisors (Trial) have been discussed and adopted by the Party Group Meeting of the Supreme People's Court. They are hereby issued. Please study them carefully and provide support and cooperation in your work.

October 12, 2009

Working Regulations of the Supreme People's Court on Special Supervisors (Trial)

With a view to further improving and perfecting the external oversight mechanism of the people's courts, safeguarding judicial impartiality, enhancing judicial credibility, and promoting the scientific development of the work of the people's courts, these Regulations are formulated in light of work requirements.

Article 1. Special Supervisors of the Supreme People's Court are persons designated by the Supreme People's Court from among deputies to the National People's Congress (NPC), members of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC), members of democratic parties, the Federation of Industry and Commerce, personages without party affiliation, experts and scholars, as well as members of the grassroots public, for the purpose of supervising the trial work, enforcement work, and team building of the Supreme People's Court, and of putting forward opinions and suggestions.

Article 2. Special Supervisors of the Supreme People's Court shall be recommended by relevant organizations, and the consent of the person concerned and his or her unit shall be obtained.

The Supreme People's Court shall issue a letter of appointment and a Certificate of Special Supervisor to the appointed Special Supervisor, and shall make the appointment public.

The term of office of a Special Supervisor of the Supreme People's Court shall be three years, and generally no more than two consecutive terms. Additional appointments may be made from time to time as required by the work.

If a Special Supervisor, during his or her term, submits a written request to resign from the post of Special Supervisor, such request shall be accepted by the Supreme People's Court, which shall then remove the person from the position.

Article 3. The work of the Special Supervisors of the Supreme People's Court shall adhere to the principles of legality, orderliness, pragmatism, and effectiveness.

Article 4. The duties of the Special Supervisors of the Supreme People's Court are:

(1) To supervise the implementation of laws, regulations, and judicial decisions by the Supreme People's Court;

(2) To supervise the impartial administration of justice by the staff of the Supreme People's Court in trial and enforcement work;

(3) To supervise the trial style, integrity and self-discipline, and compliance with judges' professional ethics of the staff of the Supreme People's Court;

(4) To supervise other relevant matters.

Article 5. The methods by which Special Supervisors of the Supreme People's Court perform their duties are:

(1) Attending relevant work meetings of the Supreme People's Court upon invitation;

(2) Participating in specialized meetings of Special Supervisors convened by the Supreme People's Court;

(3) Attending court hearings of cases tried in public as observers;

(4) Participating, upon invitation, in special inspection activities organized by the Supreme People's Court regarding trial work, enforcement work, team building, and other matters;

(5) Reflecting or forwarding criticisms, opinions, suggestions, or reporting materials from the public concerning the people's courts and their staff;

(6) Hearing and learning about the handling of matters such as opinions, suggestions, and reports that they have raised; and

(7) Other lawful and effective means of supervision.

Article 6. When carrying out their work, Special Supervisors of the Supreme People's Court shall keep secrets concerning trial and enforcement work, and shall not use their status as Special Supervisors to engage in activities inconsistent with the work of a supervisor.

Article 7. All departments of the Supreme People's Court shall actively assist, cooperate with, and support Special Supervisors in exercising their supervisory powers in accordance with these Regulations, shall seriously listen to opinions and suggestions, respond to inquiries, and promptly handle and give feedback on matters reflected or forwarded. Anyone who obstructs a Special Supervisor from performing its duties, refuses to accept supervision, or retaliates against a Special Supervisor shall be dealt with severely in accordance with relevant laws and discipline.

Article 8. The People's Supervision Office of the Supreme People's Court shall be responsible for the routine administrative work concerning the Special Supervisors.

Article 9. These Regulations shall take effect from the date of their promulgation, and the General Office of the Supreme People's Court shall be responsible for their interpretation.
